panels.rationale: Single clinical photograph from a case report of sinonasal mucocele with orbital extension; caption and article title directly support right-sided axial proptosis as the visible manifestation of paranasal sinus mucocele.
panels.attribution_text: Boualane et al. Orbital Extension of Sinonasal Mucocele Presenting as Proptosis: A Report of Two Cases.. Cureus 2026. doi:10.7759/cureus.111489. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 6.
panels.figure_caption: Unilateral axial proptosis of the right eye.
in_text_mentions: A 43-year-old woman with no significant medical history presented with a three-month history of progressive right-sided proptosis. She denied diplopia, ocular pain, decreased vision, fever, or other systemic symptoms. Visual acuity was preserved at 10/10 in both eyes. Examination revealed axial, non-pulsatile, non-reducible proptosis of the right eye without associated inflammatory signs. Ocular motility was full in all directions of gaze, intraocular pressure was within normal limits, and fundus examination was unremarkable (Figure 6). The left eye was normal.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Axial CT of a human patient showing an ethmoido-orbital fluid-filled mucocele with orbital extension, consistent with paranasal sinus mucocele. B: Coronal CT of a human patient demonstrating a frontoethmoidal mucocele with erosion of the orbital roof and intraorbital extension.
panels.attribution_text: Boualane et al. Orbital Extension of Sinonasal Mucocele Presenting as Proptosis: A Report of Two Cases.. Cureus 2026. doi:10.7759/cureus.111489. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 7.
panels.figure_caption: Computed tomography findings. (A) Coronal CT image demonstrating erosion of the anterior portion of the orbital roof (arrowhead). (B) Axial CT image showing an ethmoido-orbital fluid-filled lesion (arrow) with orbital extension. White arrow indicates the ethmoido-orbital fluid-filled lesion (mucocele). White arrowhead indicates erosion of the anterior orbital roof.
in_text_mentions: The differential diagnosis included orbital tumors, thyroid-associated orbitopathy, and sinonasal lesions with orbital extension. Computed tomography demonstrated a right frontoethmoidal mucocele with intraorbital extension through a bony defect of the anterior orbital roof consistent with pressure-related bone erosion secondary to chronic expansion of the mucocele (Figure 7).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Axial facial CT panel showing an opacified, expansile ethmoido-orbital mucocele with erosion of the medial orbital wall and orbital displacement in a patient with sinonasal mucocele; findings supported by the panel-specific caption and in-text description of Figure 3. B: Second axial facial CT panel of the same compound figure, with arrowhead marking erosion of the medial orbital wall adjacent to the mucus-filled expansile ethmoidal lesion, consistent with sinonasal mucocele with orbital extension.

in_text_mentions: Non-contrast computed tomography of the paranasal sinuses subsequently demonstrated a right frontoethmoidal expansile cystic lesion extending into the orbit with inferolateral displacement of the globe and erosion of the orbital roof and medial wall, without evidence of intracranial extension (Figure 3).

findings.evidence: Ophthalmologic examination revealed right non-axial, non-pulsatile proptosis with inferolateral displacement of the globe (Figure 1).

panels.rationale: Single clinical photograph of a real patient from a case report whose title and caption attribute the right-sided non-axial proptosis with eyelid edema and conjunctival chemosis to orbital extension of a sinonasal mucocele; the visible periorbital swelling and globe displacement match the disease-specific vocabulary findings for paranasal_sinus_mucocele. [raw subtype: orbital extension of sinonasal mucocele]
panels.attribution_text: Boualane et al. Orbital Extension of Sinonasal Mucocele Presenting as Proptosis: A Report of Two Cases.. Cureus 2026. doi:10.7759/cureus.111489. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Eyelid edema associated with conjunctival chemosis and non-axial proptosis of the right eye.
in_text_mentions: h a history of allergic rhinitis and no history of facial trauma, sinonasal surgery, diabetes, or immunosuppression presented with a one-week history of acute right-sided proptosis associated with binocular diplopia and decreased visual acuity in the right eye. He reported progressive swelling of the right eyelid and ocular discomfort but no fever, purulent nasal discharge, or systemic symptoms. Ophthalmologic examination revealed right non-axial, non-pulsatile proptosis with inferolateral displacement of the globe, associated with right upper eyelid edema and conjunctival chemosis (Figure 1).
